# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repo is

An experiment comparing how well AI builds a three.js tropical beach scene. One shared base scene (water, sky, sand, light) with 8 prop slots, where only the prop source varies:

- **A**: procedural props written by codex.
- **B**: Tripo AI GLBs, decimated in Blender.
- **C**: free library models (Poly Haven, Sketchfab, Poly Pizza).

On top of that there are an explore mode, a synced split-view compare page, a game mode, three characters (A/B/C), blind scoring, and comparison videos and slides.

Read these first:

- `PLAYBOOK.md`: the reusable process, commands and pitfalls.
- `NOTES.md`: per-feature implementation notes, written by codex.
- `REPORT.md` and `心得.md`: results.

User-facing docs are in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan); keep that.

Sibling worktrees `../beach3d-codex2` (port 5193) and `../beach3d-opus` (port 5192) hold the same pipeline re-run by other models (branches `codex2-run`, `opus-run`). They share only `assets/props.json` and the recorder hooks below.

## Commands

```sh
npx vite --port 5191 --strictPort      # dev server (npm run dev); many scripts assume 5191
npm run build                          # 5 entries: index, scene, compare, props, game → dist/ (copies assets/, report/)
node scripts/shoot.mjs <A|B|C>         # fixed-camera stills → shots/<g>/{wide,beach,closeup}.png (SwiftShader)
node scripts/shoot-props.mjs <g> [slot]   # solo prop renders → shots/<g>/props/
node scripts/verify-game.mjs           # full game regression (quests, boat, A/B/C, mobile, missing GLBs)
node scripts/verify-explore.mjs        # explore-mode regression
```

Media pipeline:

- `node scripts/record-path.mjs <g> [fps] [path.json] [outdir]`: frame-by-frame GPU render along a camera path. Uses `SCENE_URL` and `SETTLE_MS` to point at other ports.
- `scripts/record-game.mjs` and `scripts/record-walk.mjs <g>`: game and character recordings.
- Compositing: `python3 tools/make_video.py`, `tools/make_zoom.py`, `tools/compare_models.py`.

Assets and stats:

- `.venv/bin/python tools/tripo_gen.py --dry-run|<slots>|--recover <task> <slot>`: Tripo generation. Spends credits, so ask the user first.
- `tools/decimate_all.sh`: Blender headless decimation to 30k tris.
- `tools/build_stats.py` → `report/stats.json`; `tools/compare.py` → `compare/*.png`.

Blind scoring:

- `tools/blind_score.py`; set `BLIND_CONFIG` to compare other dirs.

index.html
Build a single self-contained HTML file (inline CSS and JS; the only external script is Three.js r128 from cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/thre…) called "Reef Lagoon": an interactive top-down view of a sunlit Maldives-style lagoon where the user throws sea creatures into the water and watches them swim. Output the complete file, no placeholders, no omitted sections.

CAMERA AND LAYOUT
- Perspective camera straight overhead (height ~26 world units, up vector (0,0,-1)). Fit the vertical FOV so the visible water is about ±8.4 units in the short screen direction; the long direction scales with the aspect ratio. Recompute on resize.
- The whole screen is water. One world unit is roughly 1 m at toy scale: dolphin ~2.4, white shark ~3.3, hammerhead ~3.1, orca ~4.5, humpback ~6, turtle ~1.35 shell length, manta ~1.6 length / 3.2 wingspan.

content.text:
Reef Lagoon is built and working: `index.html` is one 2,329-line file with inline CSS and JS, and Three.js r128 from cdnjs is its only external script. I tested it in headless Chromium in four setups: GPU on WebGL2, a software renderer, WebGL1, and a 360–390 px touch phone view. None of them threw page errors or broke shaders; the only console message was a 404 for the missing favicon.

**What I checked by running it**
- **Start-up:** two dolphins, a turtle, a shark and a manta are swimming, and the humpback breaches 1 s after load. It rises, rolls onto its back and backflops with the big white spray curtain, mist and expanding rings.
- **Throws:** I threw each of the 7 species from its card and took screenshots mid-flight, at entry and after settling. Each lands in its own style (shark knifes in, hammerhead corkscrews, humpback backflops, orca lands on its side, dolphin dives cleanly, turtle belly-plops, manta somersaults into a wing slap), then rights itself under water.
- **Dragging and grabbing:** dragging a card holds the creature over the water with a target ring and drops it on release. Grabbing a turtle out of the water and flinging it also works.
- **Tools:** rain (streaks, ring ripples, dimmer sun) and the whirlpool (funnel with spiral foam arms that carries creatures) both showed up; Clear makes everyone swim off.
- **Limits:** the 24-creature cap shows its toast and greys out the cards.
- **Phone layout:** all 7 cards (with short names) and the 6 tool buttons fit at 360 px wide, with no horizontal scrolling.

Everything else in the brief is implemented as specified. That includes the 90 Hz ripple simulation with absorbing edges, the caustics, the creature shadows on the floor, coral and sand, and all the creatures' swimming behaviour (breathing and spouts, shark fins cutting the surface, leaps and breaches, reactions to taps). It also includes the synthesized sound, the keyboard shortcuts, the adaptive resolution, and the toasts for errors and lost WebGL context.

**Not verified**
- **Sound:** headless Chromium can't play audio, so I couldn't listen to any of it.
- **Behaviour I didn't watch:** I didn't sit through the long-timer behaviours (whale fluke-up dives, shark fin cruising, occasional breaches). I also didn't test the WebGL context-loss toast or a phone without float textures; there the ripples are noticeably degraded and a toast says so.
- **Real devices:** everything was tested in headless Chromium only, not on an actual phone or tablet.

**Changes beyond the brief**
- I added **X** as a keyboard shortcut for Clear, since **C** is taken by Calm.
- On mobile, the cards shrink to fit the screen rather than scrolling.
- If WebGL1 lacks MAX blending, shadows fall back to additive blending.

I deleted my temporary test scripts and screenshots, so only `index.html` is left in the directory.
